saints.name: The Transfiguration of the Lord
saints.title: Feast of the Lord
saints.shortBlurb: The revelation of Christ's glory on the mountain before Peter, James, and John…
biography: Six days after Peter's confession of faith, Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, by ancient tradition Mount Tabor in Galilee, and was transfigured before them: his face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as light.

Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with him of the exodus he was to accomplish at Jerusalem, and Peter proposed three tents. A bright cloud overshadowed them, and from it the Father's voice declared: 'This is my beloved Son; listen to him.'

Peter recalled it at the end of his life: 'We were eyewitnesses of his majesty... We ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven, for we were with him on the holy mountain.' The mystery disclosed Christ's glory to strengthen the three for the scandal of the Cross.

Kept in the East from early centuries, the feast was extended to the whole Latin Church by Pope Callixtus III in 1457 and fixed on 6 August, in thanksgiving for the deliverance of Belgrade from the Turks, tidings of which had reached Rome on that day in 1456.
saints.knownFor: The manifestation of Christ's divine glory before his Passion.
